thread:
jess (ml): Heads up — pavo11b canary started yesterday. We ran per-layer int4 quant with per-channel scales; seeing a small but consistent quality dip on long-context summarization (ROUGE down ~1.8) and sporadic OOMs for sessions >2048 tokens. Repro steps attached below.

omar (infra): I captured the OOMs — pattern looks like allocator fragmentation. Main error: `cudaMalloc` failing during kv_alloc after several requests. Small stack snippet: 
```
ERROR: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
  at kv_alloc(size=...)
  at kv_insert(...)
  at forward_step(...)
```

li (serving): Probably fragmentation + large KV allocations. Canary uses legacy allocator. Suggest flip to cudaMallocAsync and enable slot compaction; also try aligning KV slabs to 2MB.

nora (evals): On the quality side, regression concentrated on prompts with lots of code blocks and long reference context. Initial bench vs our reference weights: perplexity +2.1, EM down ~0.9%. Running a broader 5k-prompt sweep now.

ram (sre): OOMs reproduce locally on 48GB A100 when sequence>2048 and batching spikes. Memory climbs steady until allocation fails. Quick mitigation: reduce default max_new_tokens to 512 and enforce a soft session cap.

jess (ml): Agreed. Also observed throughput drop when batch size >8 for this quantization profile. Proposal: default batch target 6, max_batch 12, default_max_new_tokens 512.

li (serving): Patch prepared. Changes to runtime config: 
```
runtime.config.default_max_new_tokens = 512
runtime.config.batching_target_window_ms = 20
runtime.config.batching_max_batch = 12
runtime.config.kv_align_mb = 2
allocator.use_cudamallocasync = true
slot_reserve_fraction = 0.08
```
Will roll to canary (4 hosts) for 2 hours then expand if stable.

deploy-bot: rollout started: r-2026-1765009999-1 -> canary (4/20).

omar (infra): Quick numbers from first canary hour: p50 latency 210ms (baseline 170ms), p95 480ms (baseline 410ms). Memory steady-state ~37GB, spikes up to 46GB during long sessions. No new OOMs observed in first 45m.

nora (evals): AB setup: comparing pavo11b-int4 (canary) vs pavo11b-fp16-baseline and fallbacks to pavo7b-LITE for heavy contexts. Hooking the 5k prompt suite and code-heavy subset.

li (serving): Also added emergency fallback: if allocator fails twice within 30s, route traffic to pavo11b-lite-7b-compatible. That prevents customer-visible outages.

ram (sre): Action items list: 
- li: roll patch to remaining canary hosts and add mem_frag metric (mem_frags_ratio).
- nora: finish 5k evals and post aggregated metrics.
- jess: update onboarding checklist + default params.
- omar: watch fragmentation alert threshold mem_frags_ratio > 0.12.

jess (ml): Repro bench command (use this to replicate OOM/quality locally):
```
rcli bench --model pavo11b \
  --quant perlayer-int4 \
  --max_new_tokens 1024 \
  --batch 8 \
  --seq 4096 \
  --allocator cuda_async \
  --out ./pavo11b-oom.log
```

li (serving): Note: add `--allocator=cuda_async` to mirror canary runtime. If you omit it, results will differ (legacy allocator fragments faster).

nora (evals): Preliminary results after lowering max_new_tokens to 512: ROUGE delta reduced to ~0.6 and we couldn't reproduce the OOM in 6/6 long-session repros. Full 5k-run ETA ~90m.

jess (ml): Great — if full eval confirms, we'll keep the lowered defaults for onboarding and document the quant-profile caveats (long-context quality edge cases). Hold general rollout until we have 4h canary with zero OOMs and eval pass. :thumbsup:

li (serving): FYI we'll also add a small runtime heuristic: if avg_response_length > 1500 tokens for a session, apply soft throttling (reduce max_new_tokens for subsequent requests).

omar (infra): I'll add a dashboard tile showing mem_frags_ratio, kv_alloc_rate, and cuda_async_activity. Will alert if mem_frags_ratio trends above 0.10.

ram (sre): If OOMs reappear after patch, next steps: enable compact-on-evict (kv_trim) and consider per-request prefetch window reduction. Also consider shipping small kernel tweak to align large allocs to 2MB boundaries — reduces fragmentation on heavy KV lifetimes.

jess (ml): Thanks all. Will update the onboarding doc and post a short runbook for pavo11b-int4. Will wait for nora's final eval before approving broader rollout.
